nodes.label: csrfProtection
nodes.rationale: A stateless double-submit scheme: the token is payload.hmac(secret, payload) in a __Host- cookie. Safe methods mint or refresh it; unsafe methods must present a matching cookie and header. The belt-and-suspenders option, since it runs the same-origin check too.

nodes.label: Double-submit token scheme
nodes.rationale: Three parts carry the defence and it pays to be exact about which does what: the HMAC rejects tokens this server never minted but binds a token to the secret and nothing else, so it is NOT what stops cookie planting; the __Host- cookie name is what stops planting; and the Origin/Referer gate rejects the cross-site request that would carry a planted pair.

nodes.label: __Host- cookie prefix
nodes.rationale: A browser refuses a __Host- cookie unless it is Secure, Path=/ and carries no Domain, which locks it to exactly this host: a sibling subdomain cannot write it and a plaintext origin cannot write it at all. An incompatible withCookie is rejected when the middleware is built (an OptionsError, not a per-request 500). The cookie is deliberately not HttpOnly because double-submit requires same-origin JS to read it, and any XSS able to read it already defeats every CSRF scheme.

nodes.label: Origin/Referer same-origin gate
nodes.rationale: Whole origins are compared - scheme, host and port - on both arms, so https://app.example accepts neither http://app.example nor https://app.example:8443, and an opaque Origin: null is always rejected. A request never tells you its scheme (TLS may terminate at a proxy and a forwarded scheme header is client-set), so expectedScheme supplies that missing half; it defaults to https and reads http when the Secure cookie attribute is explicitly turned off.

nodes.label: requireSameOrigin
nodes.rationale: The lightweight alternative: rejects unsafe-method requests whose Origin/Referer is not the request's own origin, with the same allowedOrigins and expectedScheme knobs. Lighter than csrfProtection but relies on the browser sending a correct Origin/Referer, and has no cookie to infer the scheme from.
